projects.name: 一个养活穷人的县
projects.name_en: A County That Supports the Poor
projects.content_zh: 清源所处的晋中地区，在清中期至民国初年是全国的金融中心。汾河以东的榆次、太谷、介休和平遥等县的县城，都因为票号云集而成为商业发达的城市。和这些城市相比，清源的商业水平无疑是大为逊色的，因为它位于汾河之西，一河之隔，便把它挡在了金融商业圈之外。在山西重商的大气候之下，清源也出了不少在外地做买卖的商人。和其他县市的晋商一样，发了财的清源商人们也喜欢在家乡大兴土木，修建豪宅。这些住宅大都位于乡村，不在县城。清源城里少有外地商号设立的分号，也无辐射外地的商号总部。清源晋商对家乡经济的贡献，不是直接在县城开设店号，而更多是通过间接的方式，比如生活和住房消费。清源的农业条件也是比不上晋中汾河以东的几个县的。汾河湾，是山西最富饶的地区。清源虽然也靠近汾河，但是它和汾河离得太近了，只剩下几里宽的狭长地块，为清源的粮食生产区。汾河东面的几个县，都是宽数十里的平地。然而，商业和农业都不发达的清源，却是一个能养活穷人的地方，因为它有几项利润不算太高、却很适合穷人谋生的行业。首先是蔬菜种植业。清源城的北、西、南三面，有大面积的菜地。这些菜地很肥沃，如果拿来种粮食，一点也不比汾河边上的农田差。但是，种蔬菜比种粮食的收益要高得多。粮食只能一年一熟，蔬菜却可以一年种三茬。这些蔬菜不但供应清源本地人，还大量出口到邻县。清源是晋中地区最重要的蔬菜基地。种植蔬菜的人，不仅有清源城外的村民，还有很多城里人。其次是葡萄种植业。清源城西的吕梁山麓，背风向阳，日照充足，昼夜温差大，再加上沙质土壤和丰富的地下水资源，很适合葡萄生长。在这里，有几十个长期以栽种葡萄为生的村庄。清源的葡萄除了供应本县及邻县外，还做成葡萄干远销东北。再次是煤炭业。同样是在清源城西的吕梁山麓，尤其是在西马峪村的郭家沟内，分布着丰富的煤矿资源。晋中汾河以东的祁县、平遥等地缺煤，每当冬季来临，这里的很多商户都要派出马车，到清源城西的煤矿来拉煤，回去当取暖的燃料。挖煤属于贱业，金融大鳄们是不屑一顾的，但是清源西山脚下的不少人却以此为生。还有熬盐业。清源的土地是盐碱地，盐分很高，其中又以城内街道上的土为最。把街上的土挖来，加水熬煮，便可得到土盐。食盐自古以来为官府控制的行业。不过，清源的土盐实在是质量不高，官府懒得管，所以清源城里便有了几十户以熬盐为生的人家。蔬菜、葡萄、煤炭和土盐都是清源重要的输出物资，其中蔬菜和葡萄的交易市场是在清源城南关小西门外的菜市坡，土盐坊都集中分布在清源城内的东湖边。煤炭的交易场所虽然不在清源城内，但拉煤的马车很多是以清源城内的旅店作为中转休息之地的。从煤窑上挣了钱的窑主和矿工们，也需要到城里来购买粮食和生活用品。这几个行业都为清源城商业做出了贡献。
projects.content_en: The Jinzhong region where Qingyuan is located was the national financial center from the mid-Qing dynasty to the early Republican period. The county towns of Yuci, Taigu, Jiexiu, and Pingyao east of the Fen River all became commercially developed cities due to the concentration of draft banks (piaohao). Compared with these cities, Qingyuan's commercial level was undoubtedly much inferior because it was located west of the Fen River, separated by a river that kept it outside the financial and commercial circle. Under the general climate of valuing commerce in Shanxi, Qingyuan also produced many merchants who did business elsewhere. Like Jin merchants from other counties, wealthy Qingyuan merchants liked to build grand residences in their hometowns. These residences were mostly located in villages, not in the county town. There were few branch offices of foreign merchant houses in Qingyuan town, nor were there headquarters of merchant houses radiating to other places. The contribution of Qingyuan Jin merchants to the local economy was not directly through opening shops in the town, but more through indirect means such as living and housing consumption. Qingyuan's agricultural conditions were also inferior to those of the counties east of the Fen River in Jinzhong. The Fen River bend is the most fertile region in Shanxi. Although Qingyuan is also close to the Fen River, it is too close to the river, leaving only a narrow strip of land a few li wide as Qingyuan's grain production area. The counties east of the Fen River all have flat land tens of li wide. However, Qingyuan, with neither developed commerce nor agriculture, was a place that could support the poor because it had several industries with not-too-high profits but very suitable for the poor to make a living. First was vegetable cultivation. To the north, west, and south of Qingyuan town, there were large areas of vegetable fields. These vegetable fields were very fertile, and if used for grain, would be no worse than the farmland along the Fen River. However, growing vegetables was much more profitable than growing grain. Grain could only be harvested once a year, while vegetables could be planted three times a year. These vegetables not only supplied local Qingyuan residents but were also exported in large quantities to neighboring counties. Qingyuan was the most important vegetable base in the Jinzhong region. Those who grew vegetables included not only villagers outside Qingyuan town but also many townspeople. Second was grape cultivation. At the foot of the Lüliang Mountains west of Qingyuan town, sheltered from the wind and facing the sun, with sufficient sunshine, large day-night temperature differences, sandy soil, and rich groundwater resources, the area was very suitable for grape growth. Here, there were dozens of villages that had long lived by growing grapes. Qingyuan grapes, besides supplying the county and neighboring counties, were also made into raisins and sold as far as Northeast China. Third was the coal industry. Also at the foot of the Lüliang Mountains west of Qingyuan town, especially in Guojiagou of Ximayu Village, rich coal resources were distributed. Counties east of the Fen River in Jinzhong, such as Qi County and Pingyao, lacked coal. Every winter, many merchants there sent horse-drawn carts to the coal mines west of Qingyuan to haul coal back for heating fuel. Coal mining was considered a lowly trade, which financial magnates disdained, but many people at the foot of the western mountains of Qingyuan made a living from it. There was also salt boiling. Qingyuan's land was saline-alkali with high salt content, especially the soil on the streets inside the town. Digging up the street soil and boiling it with water produced earth salt. Salt had been an industry controlled by the government since ancient times. However, Qingyuan's earth salt was really of low quality, and the government did not bother to control it, so there were dozens of households in Qingyuan town making a living from salt boiling. Vegetables, grapes, coal, and earth salt were all important export commodities of Qingyuan. Among them, the trading market for vegetables and grapes was at Caishipo outside the Small West Gate of the South Pass of Qingyuan town, and earth salt workshops were concentrated along the East Lake inside Qingyuan town. Although the coal trading place was not inside Qingyuan town, many coal-hauling carts used inns inside Qingyuan town as transit rest stops. Mine owners and miners who earned money from the coal mines also needed to come to town to buy grain and daily necessities. These industries all contributed to the commerce of Qingyuan town.
highlights: 清中期至民国初年晋中为全国金融中心
清源位于汾河以西，被挡在金融商业圈之外
清源晋商多在外地经商，住宅多在乡村
蔬菜一年三茬，为晋中最重要蔬菜基地
葡萄种植集中在吕梁山麓，葡萄干远销东北
煤炭分布在西马峪村郭家沟
土盐坊集中在东湖边
菜市坡为蔬菜葡萄交易市场

projects.name: 规模与格局
projects.content_zh: 清源城的规模不大。据旧志记载，其周长为六里二百步，大约相当于今天的3150米。从现在的地形图上测量，清源城东西宽约1200米，南北长约900米，面积约为0.82平方公里。这些数据都是指不包括关厢的主城的。南关、北关和西关占地各约0.23、0.04和0.07平方公里。清源主城内有一个东湖，面积约占主城之半。东湖的面积比三个关厢加起来还大，所以清源城的有效使用面积只有0.75平方公里左右。清源城的朝向是南偏西33度左右。这个朝向和汾河的流向基本上是平行的，可使清源城避开汾河水的直接冲击。清源城的形状不是华北地区常见的矩形，而是五角四阳城。所谓五角，是指清源城的轮廓是五边形。所谓四阳，是指清源城除西北边的一段城墙之外，其余四个边都可以被太阳照射到。清源城一共有七个城门。三个在主城的西、南、北面城墙上，分别称西门、南门和北门。东面城墙在历史上曾经开过东门，但终因洪水堵塞而废弃。还有四个城门，分布在南关的东、西、南三面城墙上，分别称作延昌门、小东门、小西门和小南门。不管是主城还是南关，城门都是互不正对的，也就是说，南边的门不对着北边的门，而东边的门也不对着西边的门。每个城门都对应着城内或城外的街道。主城西门外有西关大街，门内有西门街。主城南门外有南关大街，门内有南门大街。主城北门外有北关大街，门内有北门大街和察院街。小南门内有永定街。小西门内有小西门街和猪市巷。猪市巷联系着南关大街和永定街。察院街与南门大街之间也有一条街道，叫牌楼街。延昌门内有顺城街，小东门内有小东门街。这些街道，除了西门街和小东门街因处于住宅区而没有商业功能之外，其余都是布满店铺的商业街道。
projects.content_en: Qingyuan town was not large in scale. According to old gazetteers, its circumference was six li and two hundred paces, approximately equivalent to 3,150 meters today. Measured from current topographic maps, Qingyuan town is about 1,200 meters wide east-west and 900 meters long north-south, with an area of about 0.82 square kilometers. These figures refer to the main town excluding the suburban passes (guanxiang). The South Pass, North Pass, and West Pass occupy about 0.23, 0.04, and 0.07 square kilometers respectively. Inside the main town there is an East Lake, whose area accounts for about half of the main town. The area of the East Lake is larger than the three suburban passes combined, so the effective usable area of Qingyuan town is only about 0.75 square kilometers. The orientation of Qingyuan town is about 33 degrees west of south. This orientation is basically parallel to the flow direction of the Fen River, allowing Qingyuan town to avoid the direct impact of Fen River floodwaters. The shape of Qingyuan town is not the rectangle common in North China, but a 'five-corner four-sun' city. The so-called 'five corners' means the outline of Qingyuan town is a pentagon. The so-called 'four suns' means that except for a section of the city wall on the northwest side, the other four sides can all be irradiated by the sun. Qingyuan town has a total of seven city gates. Three are on the west, south, and north walls of the main town, called the West Gate, South Gate, and North Gate respectively. The east wall historically had an East Gate, but it was eventually abandoned due to flood blockage. There are four more city gates distributed on the east, west, and south walls of the South Pass, called Yanchang Gate, Small East Gate, Small West Gate, and Small South Gate respectively. Whether in the main town or the South Pass, the city gates are never directly opposite each other—that is, the south gate does not face the north gate, and the east gate does not face the west gate. Each city gate corresponds to streets inside or outside the town. Outside the main town's West Gate is West Pass Street, and inside is West Gate Street. Outside the main town's South Gate is South Pass Street, and inside is South Gate Street. Outside the main town's North Gate is North Pass Street, and inside are North Gate Street and Chayuan Street. Inside the Small South Gate is Yongding Street. Inside the Small West Gate are Small West Gate Street and Zhushi Alley. Zhushi Alley connects South Pass Street with Yongding Street. Between Chayuan Street and South Gate Street there is also a street called Pailou Street. Inside Yanchang Gate is Shuncheng Street, and inside the Small East Gate is Small East Gate Street. Among these streets, except for West Gate Street and Small East Gate Street which have no commercial function because they are in residential areas, all the rest are commercial streets lined with shops.
highlights: 周长六里二百步约3150米
主城面积0.82平方公里
东湖占主城面积之半
朝向南偏西33度与汾河平行
五角四阳城五边形轮廓
七个城门互不正对
主城三门加南关四门
商业街道布满店铺

projects.name: 清源城的建筑
projects.content_zh: 清源城在建筑上最引人注意的一个特点，是屋顶形式有着明显的阶级划分——普通住宅和店铺绝大多数采用略带斜度的传统平屋顶，而衙署、文庙、寺庙、市楼等公共建筑则用坡顶。使用坡顶的住宅不是没有，而是很少，比如延昌街的陈进士家和韩举人家以及西关务本生醋坊的正房等。住宅和店铺之所以用平屋顶，一方面是出于现实上的考虑，比如造价低廉、夏天可乘凉、秋天可晾晒粮食等；另一方面，是由于晋中地区500毫米左右的年降雨量未超过用传统平屋顶的排雨极限。而公共建筑用坡顶，除了它们不必为乘凉和晒粮食考虑外，也是有意地在制造一种身份上的差别。正因为有了那些在数量上占大多数的普通建筑的低矮平屋顶，才衬托出少量有坡顶的公共建筑的重要地位，从而造就了清源城和谐统一但又丰富多变的整体城市景观。清源城内最重要的建筑是县衙。县衙位于主城内中心偏北处，正对南门，但与南门有430米的距离。县衙前面的街道叫衙前街，其南面即为南门大街。除县衙外，比较重要的公共建筑还有文庙、学署、武庙、梗阳书院和城隍庙等，它们都分布在清源主城内的西部。这些公共建筑中，保存至今的只有文庙和武庙。文庙现存泮池、泮桥、前殿、正殿以及前后院之两侧厢房，其中正殿是清源城年代最久且级别较高的一座建筑。根据文物部门的鉴定，它是一座金代遗构。武庙即关帝庙，始建于明万历十年（1582年），建筑形制为两进四合院，大门、正殿、后殿及厢房均保存完整。武庙的大门尤为华丽，用单檐歇山顶，檐下施五踩斗拱。在那些看似平常的店铺建筑中，也有一些是值得关注的，比如醋坊、当铺和粮店。清源是山西老陈醋的发源地和主产地，清源醋坊也位列本县七坊两窑之首。清源城内曾经有几十家醋坊，保存至今的有7家。醋坊的建筑质量不高，但占地很大，布局也是按制醋的工艺流程来安排的：正房及靠近正房的厢房是制醋的作坊和放醋的库房；临街房是店面和大门；靠近临街房的厢房是住房和厨房。粮行的一大特点，是有一个很宽敞的平面接近方形的院子。众所周知，山西的乡土院落以窄长形为常见。粮行院子大而宽，是为了让运粮的马车在里面能转圈。当然，为了让马车能进入院子，粮行大门也必须够宽才行。由于马车宽1.8米左右，所以粮行的大门都是宽2米多的大型砖拱门。大拱门，是粮行在外观上区别于其他建筑的第一要素。赶马车的人在大街上远远地看见它，不用细想，就知道是粮行快到了。当铺建筑的特殊性，体现在多重防御的设计和措施上。当铺的建筑质量——表现为墙高、墙厚和用砖量等指标，都是超过普通住宅和店铺的，其目的是为了防盗。不过，当铺最特殊的防御措施是体现在另外两个地方。第一，和普通店铺为招揽顾客而在敞开临街面不同，当铺的临街面是高高的、严严实实的一堵砖墙；墙上只开一个大门，但在顶部却架设了一个出挑1米多、可以防止毛贼攀爬的屋檐，称为梯儿套檐。因为这堵墙，当铺给人的第一印象是保守的，甚至是冷冰冰的。第二，当铺内的庭院上方都安装了天网，即一层覆盖整个院子，并悬挂有铃铛的铁丝网。一旦有人触动天网，铃铛就会发出响声，惊走盗贼，也通知了当铺的工作人员。
projects.content_en: The most notable architectural feature of Qingyuan town is the obvious class division in roof forms—the vast majority of ordinary residences and shops use traditional flat roofs with a slight slope, while public buildings such as government offices, Confucian temples, temples, and market towers use pitched roofs. Residences with pitched roofs are not nonexistent but very few, such as the homes of Jinshi Chen and Juren Han on Yanchang Street, and the main room of the Wubensheng vinegar workshop in the West Pass. The reason residences and shops use flat roofs is, on the one hand, practical considerations such as low cost, summer cooling, and autumn grain drying; on the other hand, the annual rainfall of about 500 mm in the Jinzhong region does not exceed the drainage limit of traditional flat roofs. Public buildings use pitched roofs not only because they do not need to consider cooling and grain drying, but also to intentionally create a status distinction. It is precisely because of the low flat roofs of the majority of ordinary buildings that the important status of the few pitched-roof public buildings is set off, creating a harmonious, unified yet rich and varied overall urban landscape of Qingyuan town. The most important building in Qingyuan town was the county yamen. The yamen was located slightly north of the center in the main town, directly facing the South Gate but 430 meters away from it. The street in front of the yamen was called Yaqian Street, to the south of which was South Gate Street. Besides the yamen, other important public buildings included the Confucian Temple, School Office, Military Temple, Gengyang Academy, and City God Temple, all distributed in the western part of the main town. Among these public buildings, only the Confucian Temple and Military Temple survive today. The Confucian Temple preserves the Pan Pool, Pan Bridge, front hall, main hall, and side rooms on both sides of the front and rear courtyards. The main hall is the oldest and highest-grade building in Qingyuan town. According to appraisal by cultural heritage authorities, it is a Jin dynasty remnant structure. The Military Temple, also known as the Guandi Temple, was first built in the 10th year of the Wanli reign of the Ming dynasty (1582). Its architectural form is a two-courtyard siheyuan, with the gate, main hall, rear hall, and side rooms all preserved intact. The gate of the Military Temple is particularly magnificent, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof and five-step bracket sets under the eaves. Among the seemingly ordinary shop buildings, there are also some worthy of attention, such as vinegar workshops, pawnshops, and grain shops. Qingyuan is the birthplace and main production area of Shanxi mature vinegar, and Qingyuan vinegar workshops ranked first among the county's 'seven workshops and two kilns.' There were once dozens of vinegar workshops in Qingyuan town, and 7 survive today. The construction quality of vinegar workshops is not high, but they occupy large areas, and their layout is arranged according to the vinegar-making process: the main room and side rooms near the main room are the vinegar-making workshops and vinegar storage rooms; the street-facing rooms are the shop front and gate; the side rooms near the street-facing rooms are living quarters and kitchens. A major feature of grain shops is a very spacious courtyard with a nearly square plan. As is well known, vernacular courtyards in Shanxi are commonly narrow and elongated. The grain shop courtyard is large and wide to allow grain-hauling carts to turn around inside. Of course, to allow carts to enter the courtyard, the grain shop gate must also be wide enough. Since carts are about 1.8 meters wide, the gates of grain shops are large brick archways over 2 meters wide. The large archway is the primary element that distinguishes grain shops from other buildings in appearance. Carters seeing it from far down the street know immediately that a grain shop is approaching. The special nature of pawnshop architecture is reflected in multiple defense designs and measures. The construction quality of pawnshops—manifested in indicators such as wall height, wall thickness, and brick usage—exceeds that of ordinary residences and shops, with the aim of theft prevention. However, the most special defense measures of pawnshops are reflected in two other aspects. First, unlike ordinary shops that open their street front to attract customers, the street front of a pawnshop is a tall, solid brick wall; only one gate is opened in the wall, but at the top there is an overhanging eave of more than 1 meter that prevents thieves from climbing, called 'ladder-set eave' (ti'er taoyan). Because of this wall, the first impression of a pawnshop is conservative, even cold. Second, above the courtyards inside pawnshops, 'sky nets' are installed—a layer of wire mesh covering the entire courtyard with bells hung on it. Once someone touches the sky net, the bells ring, scaring away thieves and notifying the pawnshop staff.
highlights: 屋顶形式阶级划分：平民平顶公共建筑坡顶
年降雨量500毫米适合平顶
县衙位于中心偏北距南门430米
文庙正殿为金代遗构
武庙始建于明万历十年1582年
武庙单檐歇山顶五踩斗拱
醋坊七坊两窑之首存7家
粮行方形大院大拱门
当铺梯儿套檐和天网双重防御

projects.name: 从洪水到火药
projects.content_zh: 清源城和洪水的关系是尤为值得关注的。因为东临汾河，西冲白石水，旧时的清源城几乎年年都难免洪涝之害。俗语对清源洪水是这样描述的：淹西关，带北关，城里头灌了个湖滩滩。洪水对清源城的影响是多方面的。首先是城市格局。清源城的朝向之所以是南偏西33度，就是为了避开汾河水的直接冲击。清源城的东门之所以被废弃，也是因为洪水的堵塞。清源城的形状之所以是五角四阳城，而不是华北常见的矩形，同样与洪水有关——西北边的城墙被洪水冲毁后，不得不向内收缩，形成了五边形的轮廓。其次是城市水系。清源城内的东湖，并不是一个天然湖泊，而是由洪水淤积而成。东湖的形成，与清源城的防洪体系密切相关。为了抵御洪水，清源城修建了城墙、白石堰等防洪工程。洪水被城墙阻挡后，在城内低洼处淤积，形成了东湖。东湖的面积约占主城之半，对清源城的气候、景观和居民生活都产生了深远影响。第三是产业结构。洪水带来的盐碱地，使得清源城的土地不适合种粮食，但却适合熬土盐。清源城内的土盐坊都集中分布在东湖边，因为这里的土地盐分最高。土盐业虽然利润不高，但为清源城的穷人提供了谋生之道。除了洪水，火药也是清源城的一个重要产业。清源城的火药业与当地的架火民俗密切相关。架火是清源地区的一种传统民俗活动，每年春节期间举行，需要大量的火药。清源城的火药坊主要分布在城内，生产的火药除了供应本地架火使用外，还销往周边地区。火药的制作需要硝、硫磺和木炭等原料，这些原料在清源及周边地区都能获取。火药业虽然危险，但也是清源城的一个特色产业。从洪水到火药，这两个看似不相关的事物，却共同塑造了清源城的独特面貌。洪水塑造了清源城的格局和水系，催生了土盐业；火药则与民俗活动结合，形成了特色产业。这两个产业都不是高利润的行业，但却为清源城的穷人提供了谋生之道，体现了清源城作为一个养活穷人的县的特点。
projects.content_en: The relationship between Qingyuan town and floods is particularly noteworthy. Because it faces the Fen River to the east and is struck by the Baishi River to the west, old Qingyuan town suffered from floods almost every year. A folk saying describes Qingyuan floods like this: 'The West Pass is flooded, the North Pass is swept along, and the town center becomes a lakeshore.' The impact of floods on Qingyuan town was multifaceted. First was the urban layout. The reason Qingyuan town's orientation is 33 degrees west of south was to avoid the direct impact of Fen River floodwaters. The reason the East Gate of Qingyuan town was abandoned was also flood blockage. The reason Qingyuan town's shape is a 'five-corner four-sun' city rather than the rectangle common in North China is likewise related to floods—after the northwest section of the city wall was destroyed by floods, it had to be contracted inward, forming the pentagonal outline. Second was the urban water system. The East Lake inside Qingyuan town was not a natural lake but was formed by flood siltation. The formation of the East Lake was closely related to Qingyuan town's flood control system. To resist floods, Qingyuan town built flood control projects such as city walls and the Baishi Weir. After floods were blocked by the city walls, they silted up in low-lying areas inside the town, forming the East Lake. The East Lake occupies about half the area of the main town and has had a profound impact on Qingyuan town's climate, landscape, and residents' lives. Third was the industrial structure. The saline-alkali land brought by floods made Qingyuan town's land unsuitable for grain cultivation but suitable for boiling earth salt. The earth salt workshops in Qingyuan town were concentrated along the East Lake because the land here had the highest salt content. Although the earth salt industry was not highly profitable, it provided a way for the poor of Qingyuan town to make a living. Besides floods, gunpowder was also an important industry in Qingyuan town. The gunpowder industry in Qingyuan town was closely related to the local 'jiahua' (frame fireworks) folk custom. Jiahua is a traditional folk activity in the Qingyuan region held during the annual Spring Festival, requiring large amounts of gunpowder. The gunpowder workshops in Qingyuan town were mainly distributed inside the town, and the gunpowder produced was not only used for local jiahua but also sold to surrounding areas. Gunpowder production required raw materials such as saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal, all of which could be obtained in Qingyuan and surrounding areas. Although the gunpowder industry was dangerous, it was also a characteristic industry of Qingyuan town. From floods to gunpowder, these two seemingly unrelated things together shaped the unique face of Qingyuan town. Floods shaped Qingyuan town's layout and water system, giving rise to the earth salt industry; gunpowder, combined with folk activities, formed a characteristic industry. Neither of these industries was highly profitable, but both provided ways for the poor of Qingyuan town to make a living, embodying Qingyuan town's characteristic as a county that supports the poor.

projects.name: 汾河
projects.content_zh: 汾河是山西的母亲河，发源于忻州的宁武县，贯穿山西省南北，流经静乐县、古交市、太原市、清徐县、祁县、介休市、霍州市、洪洞县、临汾市、侯马市，在河津附近汇入黄河。作为黄河的第二大支流，汾河全长716公里，流域面积达39000平方公里。山西有民谣：欢欢喜喜汾河湾，凑凑付付晋东南，哭哭啼啼吕梁山，死也不出雁门关。汾河湾，是山西境内土地最肥沃的区域。不过，汾河并不是一条驯服听话的河流。它有涨有落，还时常改道，给两岸居民造成了不小的麻烦。在旧志中记载的发生在明嘉靖三十二年（1553年）和清光绪六年（1880年）之间关于汾河的事件就有8起，其中明万历二十九年（1601年）和三十一年（1603年）就发生了两次改道。由于河流的性质不可能在一个短时期内形成，所以我们有理由相信，汾河经常改道的特性决非只出现在明清时期，而应该是更早的时候就已经产生了。古人在最初决定清源城的选址时，完全可以根据之前汾河改道的历史经验，选择一个避开汾河直接冲击的位置。我们现在看到的清源城，恰好是在汾河湾的西端，也印证了这一点。汾河对清源城的影响是多方面的。首先是农业。汾河的暴涨暴落与频繁改道，大大扩展了汾河的泛滥区，从而造就了山西省内最富饶的一片土地——汾河湾。泛滥区里的土地，由于洪水携带泥沙的覆盖而成为适宜种粮的沃土。清源城东面的粮食生产区，就是汾河泛滥形成的肥沃土地。其次是交通。汾河是山西南北交通的重要通道，沿河两岸形成了许多渡口和集镇。清源城附近的汾河晚渡，是清源八景之一，图中绘有渡河的马车、推车和行人。第三是城市格局。清源城的朝向之所以是南偏西33度，就是为了避开汾河水的直接冲击。清源城的东门之所以被废弃，也是因为洪水的堵塞。
projects.content_en: The Fen River is the 'mother river' of Shanxi, originating in Ningwu County of Xinzhou, running through Shanxi from north to south, passing through Jingle County, Gujiao City, Taiyuan City, Qingxu County, Qi County, Jiexiu City, Huozhou City, Hongtong County, Linfen City, and Houma City, and joining the Yellow River near Hejin. As the second largest tributary of the Yellow River, the Fen River is 716 kilometers long with a drainage area of 39,000 square kilometers. There is a folk song in Shanxi: 'Joyful in the Fen River bend, barely making do in southeastern Shanxi, weeping in the Lüliang Mountains, never leaving Yanmen Pass even in death.' The Fen River bend is the most fertile region in Shanxi. However, the Fen River is not a tame and obedient river. It rises and falls and often changes course, causing considerable trouble for residents on both banks. Old gazetteers record 8 events related to the Fen River between the 32nd year of the Jiajing reign of the Ming dynasty (1553) and the 6th year of the Guangxu reign of the Qing dynasty (1880), including two course changes in the 29th year (1601) and 31st year (1603) of the Wanli reign. Since the nature of a river cannot form in a short period, we have reason to believe that the Fen River's frequent course changes did not only occur in the Ming and Qing dynasties but should have arisen much earlier. When the ancients first decided on the site of Qingyuan town, they could entirely have based their choice on previous historical experience of Fen River course changes, selecting a position that avoided direct impact from the Fen River. The Qingyuan town we see today is precisely at the western end of the Fen River bend, confirming this point. The Fen River's impact on Qingyuan town was multifaceted. First was agriculture. The Fen River's sudden rises and falls and frequent course changes greatly expanded its floodplain, creating the most fertile stretch of land in Shanxi—the Fen River bend. The land in the floodplain became fertile soil suitable for grain cultivation due to the silt cover carried by floods. The grain production area east of Qingyuan town is fertile land formed by Fen River flooding. Second was transportation. The Fen River was an important north-south transportation route in Shanxi, with many ferries and market towns forming along its banks. The 'Fen River Evening Ferry' near Qingyuan town was one of the Eight Sights of Qingyuan, depicted with horse-drawn carts, pushcarts, and pedestrians crossing the river. Third was urban layout. The reason Qingyuan town's orientation is 33 degrees west of south was to avoid the direct impact of Fen River floodwaters. The reason the East Gate of Qingyuan town was abandoned was also flood blockage.

projects.name: 白石河
projects.content_zh: 右枕白石，指的是清源西边有白石山。白石山是吕梁山麓的一座小山，距离清源城约5公里，海拔1080米，山高不过280米。这么一座高度和尺度都不引人注目的小山，为何在旧县志里和大名鼎鼎的汾河并列呢？原因在于，从白石山的山谷里，流出了一条对清源城意义非同寻常的河流——白石河。关于白石河，清源的旧志里有不少记载，其中大多数也是关于它泛滥成灾的。白石河频发水灾，首先是因为白石峪的地势比清源城高，清源城头顶悬河。其次，白石河在流出白石山之前已经汇集了众多溪流。地势高而源头多，自然容易形成水灾。白石河的水患如此严重，为什么古人还要选择在正对白石河的地方定居而且建城呢？在光绪版《清源乡志》对白石河水患的描述里，我们可以找到部分原因：白石河，在城西三里。源出白石峪，夏秋遇雨即涨，奔腾顷刻，直冲西城城外，各园圃并受其害，因修石坝以障之。北流支派三，南流支派二，向来并归城东南范家庄入汾。今汾河迁徙较远，任其漫溢。水性肥，土人有一水胜粪之说。近城渠道倏成倏废，唯牛家寨、柴家寨以及贾兆、油房堡等村之渠均利赖焉。这段话说明，白石河并不只有害处，它也有益于清源人的一面，那就是灌溉。文中提到的园圃，就是菜地。清源城西面是盐碱地，怎会有菜地？原来，白石河的水性肥，用来浇菜地，效果甚至不比大粪差。清源城西的很多村庄，比如牛家寨、柴家寨、贾兆、油房堡等，都是靠引白石河水来浇灌菜地的。直到今天，清源城西的六合村仍有大面积菜地，许多菜农还在以种菜为生。清源城里，也有很多种菜的人家。他们有的是全职的——不从事工商业者，基本上只能靠种菜为生；有的则是兼职的——部分行业有季节性，淡季时要靠种菜来填补收入。蔬菜种植，是清源的一个大产业。《六合村史》在解释村落形成原因时就说到：六合村……缘于白石河水冲刷，积成沼泽滩地。所谓沼泽滩地，拿今天的话说，就是湿地了，生态作用很重要。所以，白石河的好处不止灌溉，它更大的作用在于改造土地——白石河水涨时携带的大量泥沙，漫溢并堆积在清源贫瘠的盐碱地上，将其改造为可以种植蔬菜瓜果的沃土。白石沟西山口有白龙庙，在河之出水口建庙，有镇压洪水的作用。《清源乡志》卷二《八景》之白石云松图中，绘有白石河和河边的白龙庙。
projects.content_en: 'Resting the head on Baishi (White Stone)' refers to Baishi Mountain west of Qingyuan. Baishi Mountain is a small hill at the foot of the Lüliang Mountains, about 5 kilometers from Qingyuan town, with an elevation of 1,080 meters and a height of no more than 280 meters. Why should such a small hill of unremarkable height and scale be listed alongside the famous Fen River in old county gazetteers? The reason is that from the valley of Baishi Mountain flows a river of extraordinary significance to Qingyuan town—the Baishi River. There are many records about the Baishi River in old Qingyuan gazetteers, most of them also about its flooding disasters. The Baishi River frequently suffered from floods, first because the terrain of Baishi Valley is higher than Qingyuan town, with the river悬 above the town like a suspended river. Second, the Baishi River had already gathered numerous streams before flowing out of Baishi Mountain. High terrain and many sources naturally made floods easy to form. Since the Baishi River's flood damage was so severe, why did the ancients choose to settle and build a town directly facing the Baishi River? In the Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer,' we can find part of the reason in its description of Baishi River floods: 'The Baishi River is three li west of the city. It originates from Baishi Valley, rising immediately upon rain in summer and autumn, surging in an instant, directly striking outside the west city wall, harming all gardens and vegetable plots, so stone dams were built to block it. It has three northern tributaries and two southern tributaries, traditionally joining at Fanzhuang southeast of the city to enter the Fen River. Now the Fen River has migrated far away, allowing it to overflow freely. The water is fertile; locals say one watering equals manure. Channels near the city are quickly formed and quickly abandoned, only the canals of villages such as Niujiazhai, Chaijiazhai, Jiazhao, and Youfangbu benefit from it.' This passage shows that the Baishi River was not only harmful but also beneficial to Qingyuan people—that is, irrigation. The 'gardens' mentioned in the text are vegetable plots. The land west of Qingyuan town is saline-alkali; how could there be vegetable plots? It turns out that the Baishi River's water is fertile, and using it to water vegetable plots is even more effective than manure. Many villages west of Qingyuan town, such as Niujiazhai, Chaijiazhai, Jiazhao, and Youfangbu, relied on diverting Baishi River water to irrigate vegetable plots. Even today, Liuhe Village west of Qingyuan town still has large areas of vegetable fields, and many vegetable farmers still make a living from growing vegetables. There are also many vegetable-growing households in Qingyuan town. Some are full-time—those not engaged in industry and commerce basically can only make a living by growing vegetables; others are part-time—some industries are seasonal, and in the off-season they rely on growing vegetables to supplement income. Vegetable cultivation was a major industry in Qingyuan. The 'History of Liuhe Village' explained the reason for the village's formation: 'Liuhe Village...originated from Baishi River scouring, accumulating into marshy flats.' The so-called marshy flats, in today's terms, are wetlands, with important ecological functions. Therefore, the benefits of the Baishi River go beyond irrigation; its greater role is land transformation—the large amount of silt carried by the rising Baishi River overflows and accumulates on Qingyuan's barren saline-alkali land, transforming it into fertile soil suitable for growing vegetables and fruits. There is a White Dragon Temple at the west mountain mouth of Baishi Gully; building a temple at the river's outlet had the function of 'suppressing' floods. The 'White Stone Cloud Pines' scene in Volume 2 'Eight Sights' of the 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' depicts the Baishi River and the White Dragon Temple by the river.

projects.name: 三个因素
projects.content_zh: 除汾河与白石河之外，清源城的选址还和三个因素有关系。第一个因素是清源和太原的位置关系。清源是太原南面、汾河以西的一个重要集镇。清源北距太原30公里，是半天多的步行距离。行人一早从太原出发，沿着汾河西岸往南，午后即可进入清源城休息。从清源往南，是旧时的一条官道，沿途设有驿站或递铺；往西南，则是进入吕梁山区的一条重要交通线。清源西关的商业以及居民区，就是因为清源与古交、娄烦等地之间的物资交换而发展起来的。第二个因素是地下水丰富而易得。这表现在两个方面：泉水多，地下水位高。清源城及其附近，是泉水比较丰富的地方。清源之名，就是因为它西北面五里处有两眼泉——饮马泉和不老泉。因从平地流出，它们也被称作平泉。平泉有很重要的灌溉作用。平泉流碧为清源八景之一。在清源城西约三里处，有蒙泉水；城西南十里，有梁泉水港。清源城内，也有泉水，而且不止一处。比如西城根、西门洞、北城根和北门洞等处的泉眼，在清末时还都出水，20世纪50年代才枯竭。清源城内的泉水，以西南角的芹馥泉最重要。清源城内有7个面积在几亩至十几亩不等的莲花池，都是由它提供水源的。7个莲花池之间，有水渠相通。芹馥泉之水最终汇入的东湖是一个占地500余亩的大湖。清源城内外之所以出现这么多泉水，与白石河有着密切关系。频繁泛滥而且裹挟着大量泥沙的白石河，一方面把清源城外的地势逐渐抬高，使清源城内成为洼地；另一方面又不断把水渗透入地下，使清源城附近的地下水位上升，这一上一下的两相夹击，终于让一部分地下水在清源城内寻得突破口，涌出地面，形成汩汩清泉。第三个因素，是清源城西的吕梁山麓分布着众多山间溪流。除了白石河，旧志里提到的西山溪流还包括榆林沙河、马沙峪河、梁泉沙河、屠谷水、杂鱼河，贺鹅塘水、方山河和壶屏石河。这九条溪流中，有五条是明确记载在雨后要涨水的。屠谷水（即都沟河）、杂鱼河（也称泽渔河）和方山河这三条河，根据我们对当地村民的采访，在雨后也会发大水。这就意味着，在清源城以北十里到以南三十里的范围内，全都面临着雨季水灾的威胁。既如此，西山河流的防洪在清源城选址中反倒成为一个不必考虑太多的因素，因为不管在哪里都会面临同样的问题，除非放弃在这一带居住。毫无疑问，洪水可能给人们带来灾难，但在大多数情况下它还不是灭顶之灾。
projects.content_en: Besides the Fen River and Baishi River, the site selection of Qingyuan town was also related to three factors. The first factor was the positional relationship between Qingyuan and Taiyuan. Qingyuan was an important market town south of Taiyuan and west of the Fen River. Qingyuan is 30 kilometers north of Taiyuan, a little more than half a day's walk. Travelers departing from Taiyuan early in the morning, walking south along the west bank of the Fen River, could enter Qingyuan town to rest by afternoon. From Qingyuan going south was an old official road with post stations or relay stations along the way; going southwest was an important transportation line into the Lüliang Mountain area. The commerce and residential areas of Qingyuan's West Pass developed precisely because of the material exchange between Qingyuan and places such as Gujiao and Loufan. The second factor was abundant and easily accessible groundwater. This manifested in two aspects: many springs and a high groundwater level. Qingyuan town and its vicinity were places with relatively abundant springs. The name Qingyuan (Clear Source) comes from two springs five li northwest of the town—Yinma Spring (Horse-Watering Spring) and Bulao Spring (Ageless Spring). Because they flow from flat ground, they are also called Pingquan (Flat Springs). The flat springs had very important irrigation functions. 'Flat Spring Flowing Green' was one of the Eight Sights of Qingyuan. About three li west of Qingyuan town there is Meng Spring water; ten li southwest of the town there is Liang Spring water port. Inside Qingyuan town there are also springs, and more than one. For example, the spring eyes at the west city wall base, west gate cave, north city wall base, and north gate cave all still flowed in the late Qing dynasty, only drying up in the 1950s. Among the springs inside Qingyuan town, the Qinfu Spring at the southwest corner is the most important. There are 7 lotus ponds inside Qingyuan town with areas ranging from a few mu to more than ten mu, all supplied by it. Between the 7 lotus ponds, there are water channels connecting them. The East Lake, into which Qinfu Spring water ultimately flows, is a large lake covering more than 500 mu. The reason so many springs appeared inside and outside Qingyuan town is closely related to the Baishi River. The frequently flooding Baishi River, carrying large amounts of silt, on the one hand gradually raised the terrain outside Qingyuan town, making the inside of Qingyuan town a low-lying area; on the other hand, it continuously infiltrated water into the ground, raising the groundwater level near Qingyuan town. This one-up-one-down pincer movement finally allowed some groundwater to find a breakthrough inside Qingyuan town, surging out of the ground to form gurgling clear springs. The third factor was the numerous mountain streams distributed at the foot of the Lüliang Mountains west of Qingyuan town. Besides the Baishi River, the western mountain streams mentioned in old gazetteers also include Yulin Sand River, Mashayu River, Liangquan Sand River, Tugu Water, Zayu River, He'etang Water, Fangshan River, and Huping Stone River. Among these nine streams, five are explicitly recorded to rise after rain. Tugu Water (also known as Dugou River), Zayu River (also called Zeyu River), and Fangshan River, according to our interviews with local villagers, also flood heavily after rain. This means that within the range from ten li north to thirty li south of Qingyuan town, all face the threat of rainy-season floods. That being the case, flood prevention of western mountain rivers反而 became a factor that did not need much consideration in Qingyuan town's site selection, because no matter where one was, one would face the same problem, unless giving up living in this area entirely. Undoubtedly, floods could bring disaster to people, but in most cases they were not catastrophic.

chapters.name: 第三章 城墙及堤堰

projects.name: 城墙防御
projects.content_zh: 在中国古代，修筑城堡通常有两个作用：防敌和防洪。对清源而言，这两个作用都是非常重要的。清源城墙在军事防御上的重要性，与其所处的大地理环境有着密切关系。首先，清源属于农耕文明区，但距离北边的游牧民族生活区却不算远。两大民族之间的斗争，在晋中地区也留下了烙印。尤其是在明代，退居漠北的蒙元势力依然强大，不时越过长城实施侵扰。骑兵一旦突破晋北长城防线，便可顺势南下，直插晋中和华北。为了保护晋中，更为了从侧翼护卫京师，明朝在北部边疆修筑东起山海关、西至嘉峪关的外长城，又在京师西侧修筑了一道内长城，同时将山西镇列为九边之一。相比而言，大城市拥有较完善的防御体系和较强的防守力量，所以游牧民族骑兵常避开府城和州城，直扑小城市和村庄。与太原府仅数十里之遥的清源城及其周边的村庄，就属于易受游牧民族骑兵侵袭之地。其次，清源（以及整个晋中地区）还容易遭土匪和叛军袭击。这与整个华北地区的地势较平，便于土匪或叛军流窜有关，也和晋中多富商，易成盗匪劫掠目标有关。而清源西面的吕梁山区，以及更往西的陕北山区，由于生存环境恶劣，正是盗匪易出之地。比如光绪版《清源乡志》卷十六《祥异》载：崇祯六年，流寇破南关，杀居民百余；八年，流寇掠刘家山，杀城官梁凤翔；顺治六年四月初二日，交山寇破汾州，以陕西举人李昌言为伪知府……约半月，东破清源。明末清源南关有一位名叫吴用极的举人，因为组织群众抵抗流寇而捐躯，得入祀乡贤祠。上文中的崇祯六年（1633年），流寇破南关，可能就是指李自成带领的农民军，因为这一年李自成收纳了王自用的遗部，又与张献忠合兵，转战于河南、山西、陕西等地。李自成起事的地方是甘肃榆中，但他的老家却是陕北米脂县。顺治年间的交山寇，则是吕梁山区的土匪。交山寇既然把一个陕西举人奉为汾州伪知府，说明他们和陕西的关系也是很密切的。战争与匪乱频生的环境，对清源的社会文化上也产生了深层次的影响。《清源乡志》描述清源风俗，就有不甚机巧，人物劲悍、强悍好斗，勤俭少文之语。在科举成绩上，清源的武科相当好，清代还出过一个武状元——贾廷诏（1713—1765年，东于镇东高白村人，乾隆七年壬戌（1752年）科）。在出去当官的清源人中，也以武职的成绩较突出，如五代时任河中节度使的索自通、南宋时官至太尉的赵密（1094—1165年）、明朝曾率民兵抵御鞑靼的举人陈琦和清代出征大小金川并官至提督的温承弼等。清源历史上最著名的人物，当数罗贯中。罗贯中是文人，但他的名著《三国演义》讲的是军事斗争。清源民间盛行武术活动，有武术之乡之称，是形意拳、太极拳、八卦掌、长拳、少林拳、弓力拳和燕青拳的流行地。
projects.content_en: In ancient China, building castles usually served two purposes: defending against enemies and preventing floods. For Qingyuan, both functions were very important. The importance of Qingyuan's city walls in military defense was closely related to its broader geographical environment. First, Qingyuan belonged to the agricultural civilization zone but was not far from the nomadic peoples' living area to the north. The struggle between the two major ethnic groups also left its mark in the Jinzhong region. Especially in the Ming dynasty, the Mongol-Yuan forces that had retreated to the desert north remained strong and frequently crossed the Great Wall to launch raids. Once cavalry broke through the northern Shanxi Great Wall defense line, they could ride southward, penetrating directly into Jinzhong and North China. To protect Jinzhong, and even more to guard the capital from the flank, the Ming dynasty built the Outer Great Wall from Shanhaiguan in the east to Jiayuguan in the west on the northern frontier, and also built an Inner Great Wall west of the capital, while listing Shanxi Town as one of the Nine Frontier Commands. In comparison, large cities had relatively complete defense systems and strong defensive forces, so nomadic cavalry often avoided prefectural and departmental cities, pouncing directly on small cities and villages. Qingyuan town and its surrounding villages, only tens of li from Taiyuan Prefecture, belonged to areas vulnerable to nomadic cavalry raids. Second, Qingyuan (and the entire Jinzhong region) was also prone to attacks by bandits and rebel armies. This was related to the relatively flat terrain of the entire North China region, which facilitated the movement of bandits or rebel armies, and also to the fact that Jinzhong had many wealthy merchants, making it an easy target for bandit plunder. The Lüliang Mountain area west of Qingyuan, and further west the northern Shaanxi mountain area, due to harsh living environments, were precisely places where bandits easily emerged. For example, the Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' Volume 16 'Auspicious and Inauspicious Events' records: In the 6th year of Chongzhen (1633), roaming bandits broke through the South Pass, killing more than a hundred residents; in the 8th year, roaming bandits plundered Liujiashan, killing city official Liang Fengxiang; on the second day of the fourth month of the 6th year of Shunzhi (1649), Jiaoshan bandits broke through Fenzhou, making Shaanxi juren Li Changyan the fake prefect...about half a month later, they broke eastward through Qingyuan. At the end of the Ming dynasty, a juren named Wu Yongji from Qingyuan's South Pass died organizing the people to resist roaming bandits and was enshrined in the local worthies shrine. The 'roaming bandits breaking through the South Pass in the 6th year of Chongzhen (1633)' mentioned above may refer to the peasant army led by Li Zicheng, because that year Li Zicheng absorbed Wang Ziyong's remnants and joined forces with Zhang Xianzhong, fighting in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi. Li Zicheng rose in Yuzhong, Gansu, but his hometown was Mizhi County in northern Shaanxi. The Jiaoshan bandits of the Shunzhi period were bandits from the Lüliang Mountains. Since the Jiaoshan bandits made a Shaanxi juren the 'fake prefect' of Fenzhou, it shows their relationship with Shaanxi was also very close. The environment of frequent wars and banditry also had a deep impact on Qingyuan's society and culture. The 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' describing Qingyuan customs includes phrases such as 'not very clever, people are fierce and tough' and 'fierce and fond of fighting, frugal and little literary.' In imperial examination results, Qingyuan's military examinations were quite good; in the Qing dynasty it produced a military zhuangyuan (top graduate)—Jia Tingzhao (1713–1765), from Donggaobai Village, Dongyu Town, of the 1752 Qianlong renchen military examination. Among Qingyuan people who went out to serve as officials, those in military positions also had outstanding achievements, such as Suo Zitong who served as military commissioner of Hezhong in the Five Dynasties, Zhao Mi (1094–1165) who rose to grand commandant in the Southern Song, juren Chen Qi who led militia to resist the Tatars in the Ming, and Wen Chengbi who campaigned against the Greater and Lesser Jinchuan and rose to provincial commander in the Qing. The most famous figure in Qingyuan history must be Luo Guanzhong. Luo Guanzhong was a literary man, but his famous work 'Romance of the Three Kingdoms' is about military struggle. Martial arts activities are popular among Qingyuan people, and it is known as a 'hometown of martial arts,' being a popular place for Xingyi boxing, Taiji boxing, Bagua palm, Changquan, Shaolin boxing, Gongli boxing, and Yanqing boxing.
highlights: 修城堡有防敌和防洪两个作用

吕梁山区和陕北山区为盗匪易出之地
崇祯六年流寇破南关杀居民百余
明末举人吴用极组织抵抗流寇捐躯
清源风俗人物劲悍强悍好斗
清代出武状元贾廷诏乾隆七年
罗贯中著三国演义讲军事斗争
清源为武术之乡形意拳太极拳流行地

projects.name: 城墙防洪
projects.content_zh: 城墙在防洪上的作用也是显而易见的。只要不是规模特大的洪水，城墙都能拒之门外。清源城的历史上曾经修建过瓮城。瓮城既有军事防御的作用，也有防洪的功能。光绪《清源乡志》载：乾隆十八年（1753年），知县高登陛修西北两门瓮城，西瓮城长十七丈，北瓮城十二丈，壬防白石水患。这里特别强调了瓮城防白石水患的作用。城墙在防洪上也有消极的一面，这或许是初建城墙者始料不及的。白石河泛滥时携带的大量泥沙，由于有城墙阻挡，大都淤积在城外。久而久之，清源城外的地势就越来越高，而城内的地面却变化很少。这使清源城成为一个洼地，越发容易遭受水灾。城墙带来的洼地效应，还导致清源城内地下水位的抬高。地下水位抬高，固然是方便了人们打井取水，但同时也让城内很多地方成为潮湿之地，甚至影响到建筑地基的稳固性。在旧志里，就不乏公共建筑因水患而重建的记载。比如：金代创建又经元、明两代多次重修的清源文庙，到清顺治年间时已卤湿圮坏，鞠为茂草；位于县衙东侧的察院，因近水为患，顺治十六、十七年知县和羹重修二次，于光绪初年废弃；同样位于县衙东侧的布政司、按察司和府馆，顺治年间已三废其二，光绪初年时更是全部消失，其地汇为莲花池。
projects.content_en: The role of city walls in flood control was also obvious. As long as the flood was not exceptionally large, the city wall could keep it outside. In the history of Qingyuan town, barbicans (wengcheng) were once built. Barbicans had both military defense and flood control functions. The Guangxu 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' records: In the 18th year of Qianlong (1753), County Magistrate Gao Dengbi repaired the barbicans at the northwest two gates; the west barbican was seventeen zhang long, the north barbican twelve zhang, specifically to prevent Baishi River flood damage. This particularly emphasizes the barbican's function in preventing Baishi River floods. City walls also had a negative side in flood control, which perhaps the original builders did not anticipate. The large amount of silt carried by the flooding Baishi River, blocked by the city wall, mostly accumulated outside the city. Over time, the terrain outside Qingyuan town became higher and higher, while the ground inside the city changed very little. This made Qingyuan town a low-lying area, increasingly prone to floods. The 'low-lying effect' brought by the city wall also led to the rise of the groundwater level inside Qingyuan town. The rise in groundwater level, while making it convenient for people to dig wells for water, also made many places inside the city damp, even affecting the stability of building foundations. In old gazetteers, there are many records of public buildings being rebuilt due to flood damage. For example: the Qingyuan Confucian Temple, founded in the Jin dynasty and repeatedly repaired in the Yuan and Ming dynasties, had become salt-damp and ruined, overgrown with grass, by the Shunzhi period of the Qing dynasty; the Censorate (chayuan) east of the county yamen, due to proximity to water causing damage, was repaired twice by County Magistrate He Geng in the 16th and 17th years of Shunzhi, and was abandoned in the early Guangxu period; the Administration Commissioner's Office, Surveillance Commissioner's Office, and Prefect's Guesthouse, also located east of the county yamen, had two of three abandoned by the Shunzhi period, and by the early Guangxu period all had disappeared, with their sites merging into lotus ponds.
highlights: 乾隆十八年修西北两门瓮城防白石水患
西瓮城长十七丈北瓮城十二丈
城墙阻挡泥沙淤积城外抬高城外地势
清源城成为洼地越发容易遭受水灾
洼地效应导致城内地下水位抬高
地下水位高方便打井但使建筑地基潮湿
金代文庙到清顺治年间卤湿圮坏鞠为茂草

projects.name: 创建与重修
projects.content_zh: 清源最早的城，也许在春秋时期就已经出现了。清源古称梗阳，在春秋时期是魏国梗阳大夫魏戊的一个食邑。清源南关正街以南的一段，直到光绪年间还叫梗阳街，街上还曾经有过梗阳祠。隋初置清源县，新县城位于老梗阳城的北面。隋初以降，清源县的建置有过几次兴废，还曾在金代一度作为晋州的州治所在地。一般来说，等级越高的城市，越可能拥有等级较高的衙署、文庙、书院等官式建筑。清源自乾隆二十九年（1764年）降为乡，直至民国初年才恢复为县。然而，清源城有文庙、县衙、学署、梗阳书院和城隍庙等形制较高的传统建筑，原因就是它曾经有较高的行政级别。在明代，由于北方游牧民族骑兵的严重威胁，华北和中原地区的很多都经历了加宽、加高和包砖的过程，清源城也不例外。根据《清源县志》和《清源乡志》的记载：明初至明中期时的清源城墙阔一丈，基倍之，高一丈八尺；嘉靖年间重修后，城墙高至四丈，厚至三丈；万历年间，南关城墙复一律增高，并于东西城上各建敌楼一；崇祯十四年（1641年）和十六年（1643年），分别包砖一百一十丈和一百丈。根据现场测绘，清源西城墙的截面尺寸是：顶宽9.2米，底宽14～15米，高9.5米。和旧志里的数据做对比，现存城墙的厚度是相符的，高度则稍有减少，这应该是清源城的地面已经被抬高的缘故。清源不只有南关，还有西关、北关和东关。西关和北关曾经有城墙，但早在顺治年间就已经成废墟了。居住在西关和北关内的人们，靠筑石堰来抵挡白石洪水。东关，则因湖水阻隔，车不能行，地洼下，屡遭水厄，一向少人居住。旧志有开东门并建东关厢的记载，但没提到修建东关城墙之事。入清以后，尽管游牧民族的威胁已不存在，但城墙防洪和防御土匪的作用依然相当重要，而且城墙的形象是如此深入人心，以至于它已成为城市不可缺少的因素。顺治十七年（1660年），知县和羹又再次重修了清源城墙。光绪版《清源乡志》中，有一幅乡城图，反映的应该是晚清时期的清源城。从这幅图，我们可以清晰地看到清源城墙的大致构造：包砖的部分，包括七个城门和主城西半部城墙；南关的城墙和清源城东半边的城墙，依旧是土墙。此图说明，清源城在明后期几次加高、加高城墙和为城墙包砖的举动，首要目的是为了抵御白石河的洪水，其次才是军事防御。
projects.content_en: The earliest city of Qingyuan may have appeared as early as the Spring and Autumn period. Qingyuan was anciently called Gengyang, and in the Spring and Autumn period it was a fief of Wei Wu, the Gengyang dafu of the State of Wei. A section south of the main street of Qingyuan's South Pass was still called Gengyang Street until the Guangxu period, and there was once a Gengyang Shrine on the street. At the beginning of the Sui dynasty, Qingyuan County was established, with the new county town located north of the old Gengyang city. From the early Sui onward, the establishment of Qingyuan County underwent several abolitions and restorations, and it even briefly served as the seat of Jin Prefecture in the Jin dynasty. Generally speaking, the higher the rank of a city, the more likely it was to have high-ranking official buildings such as yamen, Confucian temples, and academies. Qingyuan was downgraded to a township in the 29th year of Qianlong (1764) and was not restored as a county until the early Republican period. However, Qingyuan town had high-ranking traditional buildings such as the Confucian Temple, County Yamen, School Office, Gengyang Academy, and City God Temple, precisely because it once had a higher administrative level. In the Ming dynasty, due to the serious threat of northern nomadic cavalry, many cities in North China and the Central Plains underwent processes of widening, heightening, and brick-cladding, and Qingyuan town was no exception. According to records in the 'Qingyuan County Gazetteer' and 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer': the Qingyuan city wall from early to mid-Ming was one zhang wide at the top, double that at the base, and one zhang eight chi high; after repairs in the Jiajing period, the wall reached four zhang high and three zhang thick; in the Wanli period, the South Pass wall was uniformly heightened, and one watchtower was built on each of the east and west walls; in the 14th year (1641) and 16th year (1643) of Chongzhen, 110 zhang and 100 zhang were respectively clad in brick. According to on-site surveying, the cross-sectional dimensions of Qingyuan's west city wall are: top width 9.2 meters, base width 14–15 meters, height 9.5 meters. Comparing with data in old gazetteers, the thickness of the existing wall matches, while the height is slightly reduced, which should be due to the ground level of Qingyuan town having been raised. Qingyuan had not only the South Pass but also the West Pass, North Pass, and East Pass. The West Pass and North Pass once had city walls, but they had already become ruins as early as the Shunzhi period. People living in the West Pass and North Pass relied on building stone weirs to resist Baishi floods. The East Pass, due to lake water blocking passage where carts could not travel, with low-lying ground repeatedly suffering flood disasters, had always been sparsely populated. Old gazetteers record opening the East Gate and building the East Pass suburb, but do not mention building an East Pass city wall. After entering the Qing dynasty, although the nomadic threat no longer existed, the city wall's roles in flood control and bandit defense remained quite important, and the image of the city wall was so deeply ingrained that it had become an indispensable element of the city. In the 17th year of Shunzhi (1660), County Magistrate He Geng again repaired the Qingyuan city wall. In the Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer,' there is a 'town and city map' that should reflect Qingyuan town in the late Qing period. From this map, we can clearly see the general structure of Qingyuan's city wall: the brick-clad parts include seven city gates and the western half of the main city wall; the South Pass wall and the eastern half of Qingyuan's city wall remained earthen walls. This map shows that Qingyuan town's several actions in the late Ming to heighten and brick-clad the city wall had the primary purpose of resisting Baishi River floods, with military defense as secondary.

projects.name: 城墙建筑
projects.content_zh: 清源城（不含关厢）周长为六里二百步，面积约0.83平方公里。这个规模，和一个县级行政区划是相符的。晋中的几个县城，除了太谷城和文水城之外，其他如榆次、交城、祁县与徐沟，都和清源城差不多大。和规模相比，清源城的朝向和形状更值得我们关注。清源城的朝向，是南偏西33度左右——与其说是南偏西，倒不如说是坐东北朝西南更为准确。为什么会形成这么大的偏角呢？或许，我们可以从清源城和汾河的关系上得到一定程度的解释。清源城的朝向，和汾河流向基本上是平行的，这可以让清源城避开汾河水的直接冲击。清源城内所有的建筑，不管是形制不高的住宅、商店，还是形制较高的县衙、文庙，也都因此与子午线形成25度～40度的夹角。清源城的形状，不是华北地区常见的矩形，而是五角四阳城。所谓五角，是指清源城的轮廓是五边形。所谓四阳，是指清源城除西北边的一段城墙之外，其余四个边都可以被太阳照射到。为什么古人要修一个五边形的城？答案或许在白石河。清源城的位置正对着白石河，如果清源城的西北端是一个直冲白石河的直角，那是无法长时间承受洪水冲击的。从《清源乡志》的乡城图上看，清源城一共有八个城门：四个在主城，分别是东门、西门、南门和北门；四个在南关，分别是延昌门、小东门、小西门和小南门。除南关的小西门和小东门只是个门洞外，其他六个城门上都建有城楼。其中主城北门和南门的城楼以及南关大东门的城楼都是重檐歇山顶，而西门、东门和小南门的城楼则是单檐歇山顶。主城的东门创开于明弘治二年（1489年），其后屡次被洪水堵塞，最终在清末民初时彻底废弃。其他七个城门以及城门上的城楼，均在20世纪五六十年代被拆除。清源城墙上有三样东西，是和军事防御的关系密切而与防洪关系不大的，那就是敌楼（或敌台）、雉堞和城壕。敌楼可登高望远，起料敌之用。城门上的城楼，可归入敌楼之列。雉堞是立在城墙外侧的砖垛子，其作用相当于固定的盾牌。守城军士站在雉堞后面，可躲敌军之箭，同时又可伺机从雉堞之间的空隙往城下投石或射箭。城壕是城外的沟，有水的叫护城河，无水的叫城壕。根据旧志记载，清源的城壕曾经达到一丈二尺深，也就是3.6米左右。万历十九年（1591年）修城墙，在重开东门、建东关厢的同时，也曾挑壕深阔以资守御。可以想像，要长久保持三、四米深的城壕是非常困难的，因为白石河洪水频发，且携带大量泥沙，很容易就把城壕填塞淤平了。曾经在上千年的历史长河里为清源人阻挡住无数次洪水和兵灾的清源城池，如今只剩下西城门及其北面约500米长的一段了。其余部分，都在1950年后的40余年里陆续拆除。
projects.content_en: Qingyuan town (excluding suburban passes) had a circumference of six li and two hundred paces, with an area of about 0.83 square kilometers. This scale corresponds to a county-level administrative division. Among the several county towns in Jinzhong, except for Taigu and Wenshui cities, others such as Yuci, Jiaocheng, Qi County, and Xugou were all about the same size as Qingyuan town. Compared with scale, the orientation and shape of Qingyuan town are more worthy of our attention. The orientation of Qingyuan town is about 33 degrees west of south—rather than saying south-by-west, it is more accurate to say it sits northeast facing southwest. Why was such a large angle formed? Perhaps we can get some explanation from the relationship between Qingyuan town and the Fen River. The orientation of Qingyuan town is basically parallel to the flow direction of the Fen River, which allowed Qingyuan town to avoid the direct impact of Fen River floodwaters. All buildings inside Qingyuan town, whether low-ranking residences and shops or high-ranking county yamen and Confucian Temple, thus formed angles of 25 to 40 degrees with the meridian. The shape of Qingyuan town was not the rectangle common in North China but a 'five-corner four-sun' city. The so-called 'five corners' means the outline of Qingyuan town was a pentagon. The so-called 'four suns' means that except for a section of the city wall on the northwest side, the other four sides could all be irradiated by the sun. Why did the ancients build a pentagonal city? The answer may lie in the Baishi River. Qingyuan town's position directly faces the Baishi River; if the northwest end of Qingyuan town were a right angle directly facing the Baishi River, it could not withstand flood impact for long. From the 'town and city map' in the 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer,' Qingyuan town had a total of eight city gates: four in the main city, namely East Gate, West Gate, South Gate, and North Gate; four in the South Pass, namely Yanchang Gate, Small East Gate, Small West Gate, and Small South Gate. Except for the Small West Gate and Small East Gate of the South Pass which were only gate openings, the other six city gates all had gate towers built on them. Among them, the gate towers of the main city's North Gate and South Gate, as well as the South Pass's Great East Gate, were all double-eave hip-and-gable roofs, while the gate towers of the West Gate, East Gate, and Small South Gate were single-eave hip-and-gable roofs. The main city's East Gate was first opened in the 2nd year of Hongzhi of the Ming dynasty (1489), and was subsequently repeatedly blocked by floods, finally being completely abandoned in the late Qing and early Republican period. The other seven city gates and their gate towers were all demolished in the 1950s and 1960s. There were three things on Qingyuan's city wall closely related to military defense but not much to flood control: watchtowers (or enemy platforms), crenellations, and city moats. Watchtowers allowed climbing high to see far, serving to assess the enemy. Gate towers on city gates could be classified as watchtowers. Crenellations were brick parapets standing on the outer side of the city wall, functioning like fixed shields. Defending soldiers standing behind crenellations could hide from enemy arrows while taking opportunities to throw stones or shoot arrows through gaps between crenellations. The city moat was a ditch outside the city; those with water were called moats, those without water were called city moats. According to old gazetteer records, Qingyuan's city moat once reached a depth of one zhang two chi, about 3.6 meters. In the 19th year of Wanli (1591), when repairing the city wall, while reopening the East Gate and building the East Pass suburb, the moat was also dug deeper and wider to aid defense. One can imagine that maintaining a three- or four-meter-deep city moat for long was very difficult, because Baishi River floods were frequent and carried large amounts of silt, easily filling and silting up the moat. The Qingyuan city walls that once blocked countless floods and military disasters for Qingyuan people over a thousand years of history now only remain as the West Gate and a section about 500 meters long to its north. The rest was successively demolished in the more than 40 years after 1950.

projects.name: 白石堰
projects.content_zh: 清源的防洪设施不只有城墙，还有堤堰，尤其是城西白石堰。对于清源城而言，白石堰才是洪灾中的第一道防线，城墙是第二道防线。白石堰的防洪作用实在重要，所以两部旧志都花了相当的篇幅来记录它。其中光绪版《清源乡志》卷三《桥堰》条载：白石堰，在城西一带，以障白石河。每年霖雨泛溢，直啮城垣。洪武二十四年，主簿杨克俭申准筑石坝，东西长二里，阔二丈五尺，高一丈五尺。弘治间知县仝进、李景先继修，岁以为例。顺治十八年，于城西北隅俗名吊桥河复筑土堤二百八十丈。遇河涨，城关派夫堵筑，唯迤西石坝，西关独任之。此外南北两河经流之所，北至平泉、北营界，南至西留村、北村界，石堰、土堰随圮随修，劳费滋甚。从上文可知，白石堰常坏常修，而且每次维修的劳力成本都极高。明末清初的一段时间，或许是时局动乱之故，白石堰失修，致使清源城频遭水患。顺治十八年（1661年），县令和羹重修了280丈土堤，号称坚可持久。但实际上每到水涨，依然要发动全城百姓堵筑堤堰。和大人的浮夸之辞，差点让他的一位继任者上了大当。康熙十四年（1675年）到任的清源知县储方庆，因为相信和大人修堰之后可数十年无水患的说法，狠狠地训斥了前来打报告修白石堰的下属。后经现场察看，才发现堰悉颓坏，其阔处至数十丈，唯当城之冲者尤塌毁无遗迹。不过，储县令仍不愿意发动群众修白石堰。他想出一个巧妙的方法——到西山脚的白龙庙去拜求神灵。次年春天，奇迹居然发生了。白石河改道而南去城下十里，东行放于汾河，秋水泛溢不及城郭。又过一年，奇迹再次出现——秋岁大旱，祈祷辄不应，予登山谒白龙庙而得雨者再，岁复大稔。储县令于是感慨：要是以前清源的老百姓和官老爷们早点开窍，年年来给白龙神烧香致敬，清源何至于有水患？储县令的话自然是无稽之谈，但他的文章却告诉我们白石河改道的时间是康熙十五年（1676年）。从那以后，白石堰的位置和线路也随之发生改变，清源西关及其附近人民的生活也深受影响。而原先在城西一带的一些建筑，比如社稷坛、风云雷雨山川坛和八蜡庙，也都废弃或移建他处。改道之后的白石河洪水，并不像《清源乡志》卷一疆域图中画的那样，简单地分成两条河流，而是分成五股水流，绕过清源城，在城东南方汇合之后流入汾河。相应地，白石堰也不再是一条线，而是由多条长短不一的堤堰组成的防洪系统。彻底治理白石河水患，是新中国成立之后的事了。1967年，政府采取堵绝南河、扩展北河的方法，修筑、加高了拦河坝，并挖通1400米长引河，将白石河引入汾河。工程竣工后，解除了白石河水患对县城和周围村庄的威胁。
projects.content_en: Qingyuan's flood control facilities included not only city walls but also dikes and weirs, especially the Baishi Weir west of the city. For Qingyuan town, the Baishi Weir was the first line of defense in floods, with the city wall as the second line. The flood control function of the Baishi Weir was so important that both old gazetteers devoted considerable space to recording it. The Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' Volume 3 'Bridges and Weirs' records: The Baishi Weir, located west of the city, was built to block the Baishi River. Every year during heavy rains it overflowed, directly eroding the city wall. In the 24th year of Hongwu (1391), Registrar Yang Kejian applied for and received approval to build a stone dam, two li long east-west, two zhang five chi wide, one zhang five chi high. During the Hongzhi period, County Magistrates Tong Jin and Li Jingxian successively repaired it, making it an annual practice. In the 18th year of Shunzhi (1661), an earthen dike of 280 zhang was rebuilt at the northwest corner of the city, commonly called the 'Suspension Bridge River.' When the river rose, the city and passes dispatched laborers to block and build; only the stone dam to the west was shouldered solely by the West Pass. In addition, where the north and south rivers flow, from Pingquan and Beiying boundaries in the north to Xiliucun and Beicun boundaries in the south, stone weirs and earthen weirs were repaired as they collapsed, with great labor and expense. From the above text, we can see that the Baishi Weir was frequently damaged and frequently repaired, and the labor cost of each repair was extremely high. For a period in the late Ming and early Qing, perhaps due to turbulent times, the Baishi Weir fell into disrepair, causing Qingyuan town to suffer frequent floods. In the 18th year of Shunzhi (1661), County Magistrate He Geng rebuilt a 280-zhang earthen dike, claiming it would be solid and long-lasting. But in reality, whenever waters rose, the entire city's people still had to be mobilized to block and build the dikes. Magistrate He's exaggerated words almost caused one of his successors to make a big mistake. Chu Fangqing, who took office as Qingyuan County Magistrate in the 14th year of Kangxi (1675), believing Magistrate He's claim that after repairing the weir there would be no flood damage for decades, severely reprimanded his subordinates who came to report on repairing the Baishi Weir. Later, after on-site inspection, he discovered that the weir was entirely ruined, with wide sections of several tens of zhang, and especially the part facing the city's impact had collapsed without a trace. However, Magistrate Chu was still unwilling to mobilize the people to repair the Baishi Weir. He came up with a 'clever' method—going to the White Dragon Temple at the foot of the western mountains to pray to the deity. The following spring, a miracle actually occurred. The Baishi River changed course, going south to ten li below the city, then eastward into the Fen River, so autumn floods did not reach the city walls. Another year later, the miracle appeared again—there was a severe autumn drought, prayers were not answered, but I climbed the mountain to visit the White Dragon Temple and received rain twice, and the year was again abundant. Magistrate Chu then lamented: If only the common people and officials of Qingyuan had become enlightened earlier, burning incense and paying respects to the White Dragon deity every year, how could Qingyuan have suffered floods? Magistrate Chu's words were of course nonsense, but his article tells us that the time of the Baishi River's course change was the 15th year of Kangxi (1676). From then on, the position and route of the Baishi Weir also changed accordingly, deeply affecting the lives of people in Qingyuan's West Pass and nearby areas. Some buildings originally in the western part of the city, such as the Altar of Soil and Grain, the Altar of Wind, Cloud, Thunder, Rain, Mountains and Rivers, and the Ba La Temple, were all abandoned or moved elsewhere. After the course change, Baishi River floods did not simply divide into two rivers as depicted in the territory map in Volume 1 of the 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer,' but divided into five streams, bypassing Qingyuan town, converging southeast of the city, and then flowing into the Fen River. Correspondingly, the Baishi Weir was no longer a single line but a flood control system composed of multiple dikes and weirs of varying lengths. The thorough control of Baishi River flood damage came only after the founding of New China. In 1967, the government adopted the method of blocking the South River and expanding the North River, building and heightening river-blocking dams, and digging a 1,400-meter-long diversion channel to lead the Baishi River into the Fen River. After the project was completed, the threat of Baishi River floods to the county town and surrounding villages was eliminated.

projects.name: 附：碉楼
projects.content_zh: 清源的城里人依靠城墙来保护他们的家园，乡下人又靠什么呢？在光绪版《清源乡志》卷二《八景》的平泉流碧图中，我们找到了答案——碉楼。平泉流碧图，描绘的是清源城北的平泉村，泉水四溢，山光秀美，山脚下的村庄建筑也是高矮相间、错落有致。在这些造型优美的建筑中，就有高高的碉楼。这种碉楼，曾经是清源西边山一带相当流行的一种建筑，寺庙和大户人家都可能修建。刘文炳（1876—1954年）《徐沟县民俗志》描述碉楼：又有百尺矗楼，自二层至三四层，四面各通小窗，便于远眺。上有女墙备能固守。盖为防卫套寇、流寇、交山寇时之遗物。郭维忠老人也说，清源西山一带之所以有众多碉楼，是因为吕梁山里容易出土匪。西山村民不像清源城里的老百姓有城墙可依靠，只好修建这样的碉楼来躲避强盗。西马峪村狐突庙东侧的普济寺，至今保留有一座碉楼。碉楼平面为正方形，边长约3.5米。楼高三层，通高约10米，墙厚约60厘米。一层有门无窗，墙体用大蛮石砌筑。二层和三层也只开小拱窗，墙体用青砖垒砌。东马峪村北面山腰上的香岩寺，也有一座类似的碉楼。
projects.content_en: The city people of Qingyuan relied on city walls to protect their homes; what did the country people rely on? In the 'Flat Spring Flowing Green' scene in Volume 2 'Eight Sights' of the Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer,' we found the answer—watchtowers (diaolou). The 'Flat Spring Flowing Green' scene depicts Pingquan Village north of Qingyuan town, with springs overflowing, beautiful mountain scenery, and village buildings at the foot of the mountain alternating high and low, well-arranged. Among these beautifully shaped buildings, there were tall watchtowers. This type of watchtower was once a quite popular building in the western mountain area of Qingyuan, and both temples and wealthy families might build them. Liu Wenbing (1876–1954) in 'Xugou County Folk Customs Gazetteer' describes watchtowers: There are also hundred-foot towering buildings, from two to three or four stories, with small windows on all four sides for convenient distant viewing. On top there are parapets for solid defense. They are relics from the time of defending against Tao bandits, roaming bandits, and Jiaoshan bandits. Elder Guo Weizhong also said that the reason there were many watchtowers in the western mountains of Qingyuan was because bandits easily emerged from the Lüliang Mountains. Western mountain villagers, unlike the common people in Qingyuan town who had city walls to rely on, had to build such watchtowers to躲避 bandits. Puji Temple, east of the Hutu Temple in Ximayu Village, still preserves a watchtower today. The watchtower has a square plan, with side length of about 3.5 meters. It is three stories high, with a total height of about 10 meters and wall thickness of about 60 centimeters. The first story has a door but no windows, with walls built of large rough stones. The second and third stories also only have small arched windows, with walls built of blue bricks. Xiangyan Temple on the mountainside north of Dongmayu Village also has a similar watchtower.

projects.name: 东湖形成
projects.content_zh: 东湖是清源城内的一个大型湖泊，占地达525亩，南北长710米，东西宽520米。初到清源者，无不对这个大湖啧啧称奇。清源本地人，也对东湖深感自豪。东湖夜月，名列清源八景之一。民国初年的清源县长续思文，还写过一首广为传颂的《清源风景诗》：城外青山城内湖，荷花万朵柳千株。太汾风景少颜色，唯有清源入画图。续县长说的太汾，大概相当于如今的晋中地区。其实何止晋中，就是整个华北地区，由于气候干旱，拥有大面积水体的城市也是很少见的。清源这个规模不算大的县城，怎么会出现一个半城之湖呢？答案是：东湖是清源的地势、河流、泉水和城墙诸种因素长期综合作用的结果。东临汾河、西依吕梁山的清源城，其周边地势原本就是西北略高、东南略低的平地。从筑城之日开始，清源的地形又开始发生缓慢而微妙的变化。白石河每次发大水，都携带有大量泥沙。在清源城墙的阻挡下，这些泥沙淤积在城外。年深日久，城外地面就会高过城内。西北高、东南低的地形，加上白石河泥沙的不断淤积，使得清源城内东部成为洼地。城墙和堤堰并不能完全阻挡洪水的步伐。白石河与汾河，都曾经不止一次地倒灌入清源城。在雨天，清源城内东部也会成为雨水汇集之处。从清源城西南角芹馥泉流出的泉水，在流经几个莲花池之后，最终也都流到城东。晚明知县邵莅在万历十九年（1591年）撰写的《修城记》中就说到：城内东半地势下，无居民，遇有淫雨，止为注水之区。这段话为我们确定东湖的形成时间提供了重要的参考坐标。在万历十九年（1591年），清源城内东半部虽已无人居住，但大面积的湖是尚未形成的，只有池。然而，邵莅写《修城记》的40年之后，即公元1631年，清源贡生王象极的笔下就已经出现清湖了。王象极在《清湖十景诗·序》中写道：湖，大陂也，清之有陂，居然湖矣。从未有以湖名者……因即以清湖名之。从王象极的这篇序言来看，他眼中的东湖一直就是个大陂，而不是池，所以到公元1631年时，东湖应该已经存在有一段时间了，只是还没有被人们称作东湖。杨宗新先生正是根据这一点，并结合邵莅的《修城记》和旧志里万历三十一年（1603年）汾河徙流东城下的记载，推测东湖形成于公元1605年前后。
projects.content_en: East Lake is a large lake inside Qingyuan town, covering 525 mu, 710 meters long north-south and 520 meters wide east-west. Those who first arrive in Qingyuan cannot help marveling at this large lake. Local Qingyuan people are also deeply proud of East Lake. 'East Lake Night Moon' is listed as one of the Eight Sights of Qingyuan. In the early Republican period, Qingyuan County Magistrate Xu Siwen wrote a widely praised 'Poem of Qingyuan Scenery': Green mountains outside the city, lake inside the city, ten thousand lotus flowers and a thousand willow trees. The Taiyuan-Fenyang scenery lacks color, only Qingyuan enters the painting. What Magistrate Xu called 'Tai-Fen' roughly corresponds to today's Jinzhong region. In fact, not just Jinzhong, but the entire North China region, due to arid climate, rarely has cities with large areas of water. How could Qingyuan, a county town of not particularly large scale, have a lake occupying half the city? The answer is: East Lake was the result of the long-term combined action of Qingyuan's terrain, rivers, springs, and city walls. Qingyuan town, facing the Fen River to the east and leaning on the Lüliang Mountains to the west, originally had surrounding terrain that was slightly higher in the northwest and slightly lower in the southeast. From the day the city was built, Qingyuan's terrain began to undergo slow and subtle changes. Each time the Baishi River flooded, it carried large amounts of silt. Blocked by Qingyuan's city wall, this silt accumulated outside the city. Over time, the ground outside the city became higher than inside. The northwest-high, southeast-low terrain, combined with the continuous silt accumulation from the Baishi River, made the eastern part of Qingyuan town a low-lying area. City walls and dikes could not completely stop the advance of floods. Both the Baishi River and the Fen River more than once backflowed into Qingyuan town. On rainy days, the eastern part of Qingyuan town also became a collection point for rainwater. Spring water flowing from Qinfu Spring at the southwest corner of Qingyuan town, after passing through several lotus ponds, ultimately also flowed to the east of the city. In his 'Record of Repairing the City' written in the 19th year of Wanli (1591), late Ming County Magistrate Shao Li said: The eastern half of the city has low terrain, no residents, and when there is heavy rain, it only serves as a water-filling area. This passage provides an important reference coordinate for determining the formation time of East Lake. In the 19th year of Wanli (1591), although the eastern half of Qingyuan town was already uninhabited, a large-area lake had not yet formed—there were only ponds. However, 40 years after Shao Li wrote 'Record of Repairing the City,' i.e., in 1631, the 'clear lake' already appeared in the writings of Qingyuan gongsheng (provincial graduate) Wang Xiangji. Wang Xiangji wrote in the preface to 'Ten Scenes of Clear Lake Poems': A lake is a large pond; Qingyuan having a pond is practically a lake. Never before had it been called a lake...therefore I named it Clear Lake. From Wang Xiangji's preface, the East Lake in his eyes was always a 'large pond' rather than a 'pond,' so by 1631, East Lake should have existed for some time, just not yet called 'East Lake' by people. Mr. Yang Zongxin precisely based on this point, combined with Shao Li's 'Record of Repairing the City' and the record in old gazetteers that in the 31st year of Wanli (1603) the Fen River shifted to flow under the east city wall,推测 that East Lake formed around 1605.

projects.name: 东湖的影响
projects.content_zh: 东湖形成之后，对清源城产生了一系列重要的影响。首先是导致清源城景观格局的改变。东湖出现之前，清源城的东半部已经长期不适于居住。我们可以想像一下当时的清源城：六里多长的城墙环绕之下，西半边是鳞次栉比的建筑，东半边是长满荒草的沼泽地。这无疑是一种很少见的城市面貌。如今的我们，尽可以从生态的角度去歌颂沼泽地有多么重要。但是在一个规模不大的城市里，有多达一半的面积是荒草连天的景象，无论如何是不甚美妙的。幸好，这一片沼泽地变成了宽广的湖泊。大型湖泊的景观作用是毋庸置疑的。一个具有标志性意义的事件是：东湖出现没多久，就跻身并改写了清源八景——东湖夜月取代了原先的里克遗祠。清初知县和羹亲自命名清源新八景，并各赋诗一首。其中《东湖夜月》诗写道：渚阁三清半有无，波光犹自漾冰壶。何时对影扁舟上，醉倒归筇倩鹤扶。比和县令早三十年，在东湖的名字都还没有的时候，就已经有人总结出东湖的十大景观了。明末贡生王象极的《清湖十景诗》，分别从湖山、湖月、湖舟、湖楼、湖雨、湖城、湖树、湖草、湖鸟和湖鱼这十个角度，描绘了这个大湖给他带来的景观感受。王象极还在诗序中热情洋溢地赞美了东湖：见一碧停泓，印山吞月，鱼游鸟翔，草树依依，映带远通。雨后登楼一眺，空翠无涯。城中有此胜景，概足佳也。东湖自形成之日，就成为清源城最重要的景观元素。在最近几十年，由于清源城附近的地下水位严重下降，白石河又因堤坝建成而直接流往汾河，所以东湖已无自然补给水源。没有水源的东湖，长期蒸发就会干涸，为此县政府不惜花大力气为东湖进行人工补水，让清源城继续保持这一胜景。每年正月十六的架火（清源城最隆重的节日活动），现在也已移至东湖边举行。东湖，已经成为清源人生活中一个必不可少的部分。东湖对清源城的第二个影响，是导致东门最终消失，并使东城墙趋于荒芜。清源历史上是开设过东门的，而且还形成过东关、东街以及居民区。顺治《清源县志》明确记载于明弘治二年（1489年）开东门。邵莅《修城记》也说：乞开辟东城门一座，上建城楼，内填池，外建关厢。招募乡民居住，以为保守城池之助。邵莅提到了池，说明当时东湖尚未形成，东门与城内主要街道的联系未被隔断。东门及附近居民区的消失，可能是在清末民初的一段时间（光绪《清源乡志》的东湖夜月图上仍有东门及门外居民区）。东湖对清源城的第三个影响，是催生了一系列新的行业。明末王象极已经提到湖草和湖鱼，它们是兼有景观作用和实用价值的物产。所谓湖草，其主要种类当是芦苇。芦苇可用于保土固堤；苇秆可用于建房（是做平屋顶的材料之一），也可造纸、造丝，也可用来编织席、帘等；嫩苇秆是优良饲料；嫩芽也可食用；芦花可作扫帚；花絮可填枕头；芦根可入药。至于湖鱼，其属有鲤、鲫、黄白鳝、石鳞鱼、鲇鱼、梭鱼、黄、泥鳅、小紫鱼等，种类着实不少。祁隽藻总结东湖的益处：其利蒲苇莲藕鱼，鬻盐者濒湖西居。这里提到两种更为重要的东湖物产：莲藕和土盐。土盐曾经是清源城的一个大行业，它又催生了另一个重要的行业——火药（详见本书第十章）。
projects.content_en: After East Lake formed, it produced a series of important impacts on Qingyuan town. First was the change in Qingyuan's landscape pattern. Before East Lake appeared, the eastern half of Qingyuan town had long been unsuitable for habitation. We can imagine Qingyuan town at that time: surrounded by more than six li of city walls, the western half had row upon row of buildings, while the eastern half was marshland overgrown with weeds. This was undoubtedly a rare urban appearance. Today we can sing the praises of how important marshland is from an ecological perspective. But in a city of not particularly large scale, having up to half its area as a scene of endless weeds was by no means pleasant. Fortunately, this marshland became a broad lake. The landscape function of a large lake is beyond doubt. A landmark event was: not long after East Lake appeared, it joined and rewrote the Eight Sights of Qingyuan—'East Lake Night Moon' replaced the original 'Li Ke Relic Shrine.' Early Qing County Magistrate He Geng personally named the New Eight Sights of Qingyuan and wrote a poem for each. Among them, the 'East Lake Night Moon' poem reads: Islet pavilions and three purities half present half absent, wave light still ripples like an ice pot. When shall I face my shadow on a small boat, drunk and returning, leaning on a crane-supported staff. Thirty years before Magistrate He, when the name 'East Lake' did not yet exist, someone had already summarized the ten major landscapes of East Lake. Late Ming gongsheng Wang Xiangji's 'Ten Scenes of Clear Lake Poems' depicted the landscape feelings this large lake brought him from ten angles: lake mountains, lake moon, lake boats, lake towers, lake rain, lake city, lake trees, lake grass, lake birds, and lake fish. Wang Xiangji also enthusiastically praised East Lake in the poem preface: Seeing a blue expanse of still water, imprinting mountains and swallowing the moon, fish swimming and birds soaring, grass and trees gently swaying, reflecting and connecting far away. After rain, climbing a tower and looking out, empty greenness is boundless. Having such a fine scene in the city is truly wonderful. From the day it formed, East Lake became the most important landscape element of Qingyuan town. In recent decades, due to the serious decline in groundwater level near Qingyuan town and the Baishi River flowing directly to the Fen River because of completed dikes, East Lake no longer has a natural water supply source. Without a water source, East Lake would dry up from long-term evaporation, so the county government has spared no effort to artificially replenish East Lake, allowing Qingyuan town to continue maintaining this fine scene. The annual 'frame fire' on the 16th day of the first lunar month (Qingyuan's most grand festival activity) is now also held by East Lake. East Lake has become an indispensable part of Qingyuan people's lives. The second impact of East Lake on Qingyuan town was causing the East Gate to eventually disappear and the east city wall to become desolate. Qingyuan historically had an East Gate, and even formed an East Pass, East Street, and residential area. The Shunzhi 'Qingyuan County Gazetteer' explicitly records opening the East Gate in the 2nd year of Hongzhi of the Ming dynasty (1489). Shao Li's 'Record of Repairing the City' also says: Requesting to open one east city gate, build a gate tower on top, fill the pond inside, build a pass suburb outside. Recruit villagers to live there, to aid in defending the city. Shao Li mentioned 'pond,' indicating that East Lake had not yet formed at that time, and the connection between the East Gate and the main streets inside the city was not cut off. The disappearance of the East Gate and nearby residential area may have occurred in the period from late Qing to early Republican (the 'East Lake Night Moon' map in the Guangxu 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' still shows the East Gate and residential area outside the gate). The third impact of East Lake on Qingyuan town was spawning a series of new industries. Late Ming Wang Xiangji already mentioned 'lake grass' and 'lake fish,' which were products with both landscape and practical value. The so-called 'lake grass,' its main species should be reeds. Reeds can be used for soil conservation and dike stabilization; reed stalks can be used for building houses (one of the materials for flat roofs), paper-making, silk-making, and weaving mats and curtains; tender reed stalks are excellent fodder; tender shoots are edible; reed flowers can make brooms; reed catkins can fill pillows; reed roots can be used as medicine. As for lake fish, their species include carp, crucian carp, yellow and white eel, stone-scale fish, catfish, mullet, yellow, loach, small purple fish, etc., quite a few species. Qi Juanzao summarized the benefits of East Lake: Its benefits are cattails, reeds, lotus roots, and fish; salt sellers live by the west of the lake. Here two more important East Lake products are mentioned: lotus roots and earth salt. Earth salt was once a major industry in Qingyuan town, and it spawned another important industry—gunpowder (see Chapter 10 for details).

projects.name: 龙门、灌稼渠
projects.content_zh: 龙门和灌稼渠是东湖的排水口和排水通道，位于清源城的东南角。关于龙门和灌稼渠，顺治版《清源县志》和光绪版《清源乡志》均有记载，其中《清源乡志》卷三《水利》说：灌稼渠，一名官渠，在城外东南隅，以泄东湖水，闸口名龙门，上建奎楼。道光初，徐沟知县邓移水口于东门左，旧龙门、奎楼俱废。道光二十年、二十四年，白石水涨，挟汾河直从水口倒灌入城，势危甚，水口仍移旧址，止建石闸。渠路向由罗家庄、范家庄入汾，今汾河东徙，渠水无所归，漫溢于范家庄旧河身。每岁春夏之交，城关暨五十七村分按尺寸挑浚，以泄水患。乡城地势，外高内洼，疏泄不易，因势利导，亟宜更筹善策也。旧志的信息说明了下面几个问题：（1）顺治年间，城东南角的出水口和城外的灌稼渠就已经存在了，排水效果似乎不是很差（《清源县志》没提这方面有麻烦）。光绪初年，出水口和灌稼渠的排水就成了大问题，它们在发大水时根本不起作用。（2）汾河改道，向东移远了数里，东湖水变得更难向外疏浚了。分析原因：一是距离太远，不便修沟渠，只好任水漫溢；二是外高内低的地势，导致出水口沦为入水口。清源的地势是西北高、东南低，正常情况下清源东城外的地势应该比城内略低。出现清源东城外地势比城内高的现象，只能用城外有逐渐堆积的淤泥来解释。这些淤泥，可能是汾河带来的，也可能是拜白石河泛滥所赐。（3）光绪年间，真正有效的东湖排洪之法是人工挑水。每年春夏之交的雨季，城关和城外57个村的所有居民，都要按事前分好的任务，到东湖来挑水。如此耗费人力的原始办法，自然是不理想的，但县官面对积重难返的东湖水难题，也别无良策。（4）道光初年，曾将龙门北移至东门旁边，但由于这样导致洪灾更严重，不得不将出水口移回原址。为什么会想到将龙门北移呢？有说法是出于科举风水上的考虑：堵住东南角，不让文气流走，就可以提高清源的科举成绩。（5）龙门之上，原先是有一座楼阁建筑的，名为奎楼。奎楼供奎星。奎星也称魁星，是主管文运（尤指科举考试）的神。奎楼建在城之巽位（即东南），也是为了改变一城之风水格局，使当地士子在科举考试中取得好成绩。据晚清清源举人吴用极撰写的《创建奎星楼记》，该楼建于白余庆任县令的泰昌元年至天启四年（1620—1624年）之间，其初衷便是慨邑之人文不竞，科第寥简。这座奎楼毁于龙门北移的道光初年，在龙门于道光晚期移回东南角时，也没重建。后来清源人又重建了一座奎楼，并更名为文源楼。文源楼于文化大革命期间（1966—1976年）拆除，但它的真实形象却留在了一张20世纪50年代的老照片上——一座六转角的两层楼阁。20世纪80年代，清源人曾经集资仿建了这样一座楼阁。1998年，这座楼阁也被拆除，取而代之的是一座高50米的大型仿古建筑。
projects.content_en: Dragon Gate and Guanjia Canal were the drainage outlet and drainage channel of East Lake, located at the southeast corner of Qingyuan town. Regarding Dragon Gate and Guanjia Canal, both the Shunzhi edition of 'Qingyuan County Gazetteer' and the Guangxu edition of 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' have records. Among them, 'Qingyuan Township Gazetteer' Volume 3 'Water Conservancy' says: Guanjia Canal, also called Official Canal, is at the southeast corner outside the city, to discharge East Lake water. The gate is called Dragon Gate, with a Kui Tower built on top. In the early Daoguang period, Xugou County Magistrate Deng moved the water outlet to the left of the East Gate, and the old Dragon Gate and Kui Tower were both abandoned. In the 20th and 24th years of Daoguang, Baishi River water rose, carrying the Fen River to backflow directly into the city from the water outlet, with very dangerous momentum; the water outlet was moved back to the original site, and only a stone sluice was built. The canal route originally entered the Fen River through Luojiazhuang and Fanjiazhuang; now the Fen River has shifted east, so canal water has nowhere to go, overflowing in the old riverbed of Fanjiazhuang. Every year at the turn of spring and summer, the city pass and 57 villages outside divide tasks by measurement to dredge, in order to discharge flood damage. The terrain of the town and countryside is high outside and low inside, making drainage difficult; guiding according to the situation, it is urgent to plan better strategies. The information from old gazetteers explains the following issues: (1) During the Shunzhi period, the water outlet at the southeast corner of the city and the Guanjia Canal outside the city already existed, and the drainage effect seemed not too bad (the 'Qingyuan County Gazetteer' does not mention problems in this regard). In the early Guangxu period, drainage from the water outlet and Guanjia Canal became a major problem—they simply did not work during major floods. (2) The Fen River changed course, shifting eastward by several li, making East Lake water even harder to discharge outward. Analysis of reasons: first, the distance was too far, making it inconvenient to build canals, so water was allowed to overflow; second, the high-outside-low-inside terrain caused the water outlet to become a water inlet. Qingyuan's terrain is high in the northwest and low in the southeast; under normal circumstances, the terrain outside Qingyuan's east city should be slightly lower than inside. The phenomenon of terrain outside Qingyuan's east city being higher than inside can only be explained by gradually accumulated silt outside the city. This silt may have been brought by the Fen River, or may be due to Baishi River flooding. (3) During the Guangxu period, the truly effective method of East Lake flood discharge was manual water carrying. Every year during the rainy season at the turn of spring and summer, all residents of the city pass and 57 villages outside had to come to East Lake to carry water according to pre-assigned tasks. Such a labor-intensive primitive method was naturally not ideal, but county officials facing the entrenched East Lake water problem had no other good strategy. (4) In the early Daoguang period, Dragon Gate was once moved north to beside the East Gate, but because this caused even more severe floods, the water outlet had to be moved back to the original site. Why was moving Dragon Gate north considered? There is a说法 that it was out of imperial examination fengshui considerations: blocking the southeast corner to prevent literary qi from flowing away could improve Qingyuan's imperial examination results. (5) Above Dragon Gate, there was originally a tower building called Kui Tower. Kui Tower enshrined Kui Star. Kui Star, also called Kuixing, was the deity in charge of literary fortune (especially imperial examinations). Building Kui Tower at the city's xun position (i.e., southeast) was also to change the city's fengshui pattern, enabling local scholars to achieve good results in imperial examinations. According to 'Record of Establishing Kuixing Tower' written by late Qing Qingyuan juren Wu Yongji, the tower was built between the 1st year of Taichang and the 4th year of Tianqi (1620–1624) when Bai Yuqing was county magistrate, with the original intention of lamenting that the county's literary talent was not competitive and imperial examination successes were few. This Kui Tower was destroyed in the early Daoguang period when Dragon Gate was moved north, and when Dragon Gate was moved back to the southeast corner in the late Daoguang period, it was not rebuilt. Later, Qingyuan people rebuilt a Kui Tower and renamed it Wenyuan Tower (Literary Source Tower). Wenyuan Tower was demolished during the Cultural Revolution (1966–1976), but its true image remains in an old photograph from the 1950s—a two-story tower with six corners. In the 1980s, Qingyuan people raised funds to仿建 such a tower. In 1998, this tower was also demolished, replaced by a large antique building 50 meters high.
